issues.reason: The instruction set routes a capability generic over a kind categorically away from this form — "a capability generic (\"Ns can V\") ... not this event-rule form ... Only a non-modal verbal generic (\"birds fly\") takes the event rule" — and (Can e) is reserved for "a specific subject's ability", so (Can (sk_count $x)) inside an Implication over the kind keeper is the excluded routing, not gap territory.

gaps_confirmed: The mandated (Inheritance <kind> (can <action>)) property form has only a compound-action slot: it cannot carry the definite group object "the sky-cats" (the compound's Patient can name only the kind sky_cat, severing the link to sk_group_1) nor the adverb "exactly", so no licensed form encodes this sentence in full.
defect_summary: The compliant routing is the reified kind property (: keeper_cant_count (Inheritance keeper (can count_sky_cat)) (STV 0.0 0.99)) with its compound-action decomposition (Inheritance count_sky_cat count) (Patient count_sky_cat sky_cat) — but that form silently drops "exactly", which widens the denial from "cannot count them exactly" to "cannot count them at all", and it cannot reference the definite group sk_group_1; the instruction set therefore licenses NO fully compliant form for this sentence's content, which is the gap recorded above.
notes: sky_cat with its cat genus, the definite plural as a top-level GroupOf witness, Theme for the counted set and the absent QuantifierPhrase for plain "not" are all right, and (Manner … exactly) is defensible as a how-adverb rather than a degree adverb, so I do not treat it as a second fault.
